If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for mid-horizon (days 10–20) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early-horizon (days 1–5) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

When sentiment swings from positive to negative within 3 days, shift forecast peak earlier (by 2–4 days) and reduce late-horizon (days 20–30) volatility by 10–20%.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.3–0.7% upward bias to forecast for late-horizon (days 20–30) to reflect sustained momentum.

If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% for mid-horizon (days 10–20) to reflect weakening momentum.

If sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.33–0.67) and forecast shows volatility, apply smoothing filter to reduce 1–2% peak-to-trough amplitude in forecast for all horizons to avoid overfitting.
